subject: Acme Bank - Eval setup & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmebank.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Ethan Park <ethan@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: Acme Bank - Eval setup & next steps

Hi Jordan - thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps to get the model evals running on Redwood: 

TL;DR: We recommend starting with two candidate variants for your summary/QA workload: Redwood-vicuna-13B-q4 (higher quality) and Redwood-7B-int8 (lower cost, faster). We'll run a prioritized eval suite on a 100-500 row sample you provide and deliver a report with metric breakdowns, sample outputs, and regression signals.

Recommended models & why:
- Redwood-vicuna-13B-q4: best quality for long-form summaries and sensitive finance language; expect higher token-cost but stronger factuality.
- Redwood-7B-int8: good baseline for throughput-sensitive routes (lower latency, lower cost).

Benchmarks & reference tests:
- Redwood finance benchmark (retrieval+QA): https://redwood.ai/evals/benchmarks/finance-retrieval-2026
- Internal prompt set for banking summaries (attached: prompt_set_acme.md)

Eval setup (what we need from you):
1) A sample dataset CSV (100-500 rows preferred) with these columns: id, customer_id (hashed), prompt, expected_answer, label_type (extractive/abstractive), priority_flag. See attached sample: acme_eval_dataset_sample.csv
2) A short description of scoring criteria: we recommend automatic metrics (ROUGE-L for summaries, exact/partial match for QA), semantic similarity (embedding-based cosine) and a small human-eval pool for safety/regression checks.
3) PII guidance: please hash or pseudonymize customer_id and any direct identifiers; we can also run the evals in a Private sandbox if you prefer no external exposure.

Next steps / timeline:
- You upload sample dataset + SOW/PO by EOD Wed Feb 24
- Redwood runs the evals in our sandbox (3 business days) and shares a results report + artifacts (outputs, failure cases)
- Follow-up sync to review results and recommend production variants

Cost ballpark: initial sandbox eval run typically consumes ~3-5k Redwood credits depending on dataset size and model choice. We'll provide a precise estimate once you share the sample.

Attachments: acme_eval_dataset_sample.csv (CSV), prompt_set_acme.md (MD), redwood_eval_instructions.pdf (PDF)

Would you be able to share the sample dataset by EOD Wed (24th)? Happy to hop on a short 30-min walkthrough if helpful.

Thanks -
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions

Great questions - answers inline below. Also attaching a short one-pager SOW that Procurement can use.

1) PII guidance:
- Please remove/irreversibly hash direct identifiers (account numbers, SSNs). Transaction descriptions can be left but we recommend token-level masking for any obvious names. If you prefer, we can run the eval in a Private sandbox or on your Dedicated capacity so raw values never leave your network.

2) Latency expectations (p95, 256-token response):
- Hosted (shared pool): Redwood-7B-int8 ~ 220-300 ms per token p95 depending on concurrency; 256-token response typically ~55-75ms *per token* aggregated - plan on ~6-18s per request depending on batching and concurrency.
- Dedicated: expect ~30-50% lower latency at comparable batch sizes; for strict SLOs we recommend Dedicated with burst capacity.

3) Labels & dataset format:
- Single CSV is fine as long as you include a label_type column. Sample header (first row):
  id,customer_id,prompt,expected_answer,label_type,priority_flag
- For extractive labels use exact text expected_answer; for abstractive provide a short canonical summary and we'll include human-eval sampling.

4) Who runs the evals:
- Redwood will run the evals in the sandbox for this initial engagement (we'll provision a temporary project and share results + artifacts). If you want to self-run later we provide the eval toolkit and a runbook.

5) SOW & cost:
- Attaching a one-pager SOW and rough cost estimate (redwood_eval_instructions.pdf). Ballpark: 3-5k credits for initial run; final quote after we see sample size and average output length.

Next steps: once you confirm PII approach and upload the sample CSV to the Drive link below, we'll queue the eval and target a 3 business day turnaround.

Upload link (shared folder): https://drive.redwood.com/teams/acme-evals/ACB-4721
HubSpot deal (for procurement reference): https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/ACB-4721

If useful, Neha (cc) and Ethan (cc) can join a quick technical call to walk through dataset formatting and scoring thresholds.

Best,
Marissa
